record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: In even characteristic, is every egg O(n, 2n, q) automatically good, in the sense that some element π has the property that every 3n − 1 dimensional space generated by π and two other distinct egg elements contains exactly q^n + 1 egg elements?

evidence.quote: 7. Is O(n, 2n, q), with q even, always good?
For n = m such a set O(n, m, q) is called a pseudo-ovoid or a generalized ovoid or an [n − 1]-ovoid or an egg of PG(2n + m − 1, q); a [0]-ovoid of PG(3, q) is just an ovoid of PG(3, q).

An egg O = O(n, 2n, q), respectively a TGQ T(O), is called good at an element π ∈ O if for every two distinct elements π and π′ of O − {π} the (3n − 1)-dimensional space < π, π′, π > contains exactly qn + 1 elements of O; in such a case π is called a good element of O.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be a power of 2 and let n be a positive integer. Work in the projective space PG(4n−1, q). A family O = {π_0, π_1, …, π_{q^{2n}}} of q^{2n}+1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(4n−1, q) is called an egg O(n, 2n, q) if:
(i) any three distinct elements of O span a (3n−1)-dimensional subspace; and
(ii) for each element π_i ∈ O there exists a (3n−1)-dimensional subspace T_i (the tangent space) containing π_i and disjoint from every other π_j ∈ O with j ≠ i.

An element π ∈ O is said to be good if for every pair of distinct elements π′, π″ ∈ O \ {π} the (3n−1)-dimensional subspace ⟨π, π′, π″⟩ contains exactly q^n + 1 elements of O. The egg O is called good if it has at least one good element.

Question: For every positive integer n and every power q of 2, is every egg O(n, 2n, q) in PG(4n−1, q) good?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every egg O(n, 2n, q) in even characteristic is good appears to remain open. Recent work (e.g., J.A. Thas and K. Thas, "Translation Generalized Quadrangles in Even Characteristic", Combinatorica 26 (2006), and subsequent papers on eggs containing a pseudo-conic) gives only partial characterizations (e.g., classicality follows when the egg is good and contains a pseudo-conic). No source found establishes goodness of all even-characteristic eggs, nor a counterexample.

status_evidence.title: Translation Generalized Quadrangles In Even Characteristic
status_evidence.snippet: New characterizations of T_2(O) and Q(4,q) in even characteristic; partial results on eggs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress in even characteristic concerns only partial characterizations, not full goodness of all eggs.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n−1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-conic
status_evidence.snippet: An even-characteristic egg is classical iff it is good at an element and contains a pseudo-conic, or contains two intersecting pseudo-conics.
status_evidence.claim: Conditional results assume goodness; the general goodness question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: On Eggs and Translation Generalised Quadrangles
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of eggs and TGQs lists goodness of even-characteristic eggs among open research directions.
status_evidence.claim: Goodness of all O(n,2n,q) with q even is listed as an open problem.
